title: Bayesian latency calibration & reservoir-sampling scratch
content:
Goal: experiment with a lightweight, online reservoir sampler + Bayesian calibration to produce stable p95/p99 estimates with fewer traces (target: <5k samples) and while preserving sensitivity to microbursts. Secondary: correlate tail shifts with KV-cache hit-rate and batch size changes.

Motivation and constraints:
- Production cost: tracing every request is expensive. We need a trace selection policy that keeps tail fidelity without capturing a huge volume.
- Typical run-time constraints: 500–2k QPS per node, bursty ingress with short microbursts (50–300ms windows).
- Observability goal: fast signal for SLO regressions (within 5 minutes).

Mechanics (what I implemented):
1) Reservoir sampler per-worker (size N=1024) with TTL slots (rotate every 30s) so that very recent bursts get higher chance by time-weighted replacement.
2) Each sampled trace emits {latency_ms, batch_size, kv_hit, model_variant, warm_cache_flag}. Samples are aggregated into a 5-minute sliding window for Bayesian quantile estimation.
3) Bayesian estimator: use a simple beta-binomial posterior on exceedance counts for thresholds (t = 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000ms). Posterior summarized by median and 90% credible interval. Rationale: robust to small n and gives uncertainty bars.
4) Sampling heuristic: base_prob = 0.01; if latency>250ms or kv_hit==false => multiply prob by 5; during detected microburst (ingress rate > 2x baseline) temp multiplier 3. Ensure we still cap sampled rate to ~1% overall.

Test harness & environment:
- Cluster: small dev pool, 4 GPU nodes (A100s), 16 worker processes per node, each process runs local sampler.
- Workload generator: custom k6 script generating request size distribution: 60% short (avg tokens 24), 30% medium (avg 128), 10% long (avg 512). Overlay Poisson arrivals with periodic bursts (sawtooth every 120s, 20s wide).
- Two model variants: v1 float32 baseline, v1-q4 heavy quantized path. Use routing split 80/20.
- Cache priming: run synthetic prefix requests for 60s pre-run for 'warm' experiments; for 'cold' runs we flush kv-cache.

Runs performed (summary):
- Run A (warm cache, reservoir N=1024, base_prob 0.01): 30m, avg QPS 1200, bursts to 3000 qps for 20s.
- Run B (cold cache, reservoir N=1024, same prob): 30m, same traffic.
- Run C (warm cache, reservoir N=4096 - over-sample): 15m, evaluate diminishing returns.
- Run D (warm cache, smarter weighting: TTL=10s, heavier time decay): 15m.

Key results (aggregated) - extracted from sampled traces and full tail-run validation (we also recorded full traces for 2 short windows to validate):
- p50/p95/p99 (validation window with full traces):
  - Run A (warm): p50=42ms, p95=119ms, p99=265ms
  - Run B (cold): p50=68ms, p95=210ms, p99=580ms
  - Run C (warm, big reservoir): p50=41ms, p95=116ms, p99=260ms
  - Run D (warm, decay): p50=44ms, p95=112ms, p99=248ms

Sampler fidelity (Bayesian median posterior vs validation):
- With N=1024 and base_prob 0.01: p95 median error ~ +6% absolute (overestimate) with credible interval width ~ ±12% at 90% CI. p99 median error ~ +15% absolute.
- Increasing reservoir to 4096 reduces p99 error to ~ +6% and CI width narrows by ~2x.
- Time-weighting (Run D) improves responsiveness to microbursts: reduces lag in posterior shift from ~45s -> ~18s (i.e., detects tail jump earlier).

KV-cache correlation:
- Observed strong correlation between kv_hit=false and long tails. In Run B (cold): 68% of p99 traces had kv_hit=false. Warm runs showed kv_hit=false in ~22% of p99 traces.
- Suggestion: include kv-cache miss flag in routing heuristic to trigger higher sampling prob.

Batching observations:
- Larger batch_size correlates to a multi-modal latency distribution; some batches add 50–120ms extra. The sampler captured those with higher weight when we included batch_size as multiplicative factor in the sampling prob (batch_size>8 => x2 sampling).

Quick ASCII chart (p99 median over time for Run A, 5m buckets):
[time]  00:00 |====| 00:05 |=====| 00:10 |========| 00:15 |=============| 00:20 |========| 00:25 |===| 00:30
[p99]   220ms    230ms    260ms      340ms         510ms          280ms    240ms

Operational notes / gotchas:
- Reservoir per-worker avoids central contention but introduces variance across workers; need to stratify by worker when aggregating or use worker-weighted merging.
- TTL rotation helps short bursts get represented but can bias against low-frequency long tails: keep a small global 'rare-trace' queue (size 64) that accepts extremely high-latency samples for long-term preservation.
- Bayesian thresholds are cheap but coarse; if we need continuous quantile estimation consider P^2 or t-digest appended to sampled traces. However that increases memory/merge cost.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- A/B the sampler heuristic with an adaptive base_prob tuned by ingress variance metric (observe sample rate drift and tail fidelity).
- Implement worker-weighted merge and run longer 3h job to see behavior across diurnal changes.
- Add a tiny local t-digest per-worker updated only for sampled traces to produce continuous estimates; compare to Bayesian exceedance approach.
- Evaluate overhead: measured sampling + emit added ~0.4ms median CPU overhead per request in these experiments (prof snapshot attached in PR).

Notes for integration:
- Add feature flag 'bayes_sampler_v1' with config: reservoir_size, ttl_seconds, base_prob, burst_multiplier, kv_miss_multiplier, batch_multiplier. Default conservative settings: 1024, 30s, 0.01, 3x, 5x, 2x.
- Telemetry hooks: emit sample_count, posterior_mean_p95, posterior_ci90_p95 as metrics every 30s.

Personal conclusion (scratch):
- Reservoir sampling + Bayesian exceedance gives a sweet spot: low emit volume and interpretable uncertainty bands. Time-weighting is crucial for microburst sensitivity. For production, go with N=2048 and TTL=20s as a starting compromise; tune after 24–72h stability run.

Raw commands used (dev harness):
- traffic: k6 run --vus 400 --duration 30m bursts.js --out json=burstA.json
- sampler instrument: python tools/run_local_sampler.py --reservoir 1024 --ttl 30 --out samples/runA.json
- offline validation: python tools/validate_traces.py --full-traces full-window.json --samples samples/runA.json --report reports/runA-compare.md

Scratch: keep an eye on interplay with autoscaler (scale-down during lull eats sampler state). Need state-drain hooks or persist reservoir snapshot every 60s to central store (small proof-of-concept acceptable).

-- Finn (quick log, will flesh into PR notes once we pick a config)
